topicName: Always On Availability Groups Architecture and Configuration
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Always On Availability Groups Architecture and Configuration in Microsoft SQL Server"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always On Availability Groups (AG) is an enterprise-level high availability and disaster recovery solution introduced in SQL Server. It maximizes the availability of a set of user databases for an enterprise. This tutorial covers the underlying architecture and provides a step-by-step configuration guide."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Architecture Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"An Availability Group supports a failover environment for a discrete set of user databases, known as availability databases, that fail over together. An AG supports a set of read-write primary databases and one to eight sets of corresponding secondary databases."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Primary Replica: The instance of SQL Server that hosts the primary databases, serving read-write traffic and sending transaction log records to secondary replicas."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Secondary Replicas: One or more instances of SQL Server that host secondary databases, maintaining data synchronization through log application."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Windows Server Failover Clustering (WSFC): The underlying clustering infrastructure that monitors health and manages failover orchestration."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites for Configuration"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Nodes must be joined to the same Active Directory domain."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"WSFC must be installed and running across all participating nodes."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SQL Server instances must be running under a domain account with appropriate permissions."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always On High Availability feature must be enabled via SQL Server Configuration Manager on all nodes."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enable Always On Availability Groups"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Open SQL Server Configuration Manager, right-click SQL Server Services, select Properties, navigate to the Always On High Availability tab, and check the box to Enable Always On Availability Groups. Restart the SQL Server service."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Create Database Master Key and Endpoints"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Execute the following T-SQL script on all replicas to create the database master key and the endpoint required for mirroring communication."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'StrongMasterKeyPassword123!';
CREATE ENDPOINT [Hadr_Endpoint]
STATE=STARTED
AS TCP (LISTENER_PORT = 5022)
FOR DATABASE_MIRRORING (ROLE = ALL, ENCRYPTION = REQUIRED ALGORITHM AES);"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Create the Availability Group"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensure the database is in the Full recovery model and a full backup has been taken. Run the following T-SQL script on the primary replica to create the AG."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"CREATE AVAILABILITY GROUP [AG01]
WITH (AUTOMATED_BACKUP_PREFERENCE = PRIMARY)
FOR DATABASE [SalesDB]
REPLICA ON 
N'SQLNode1' WITH (
    ENDPOINT_URL = N'TCP://SQLNode1.domain.com:5022',
    AVAILABILITY_MODE = SYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT,
    FAILOVER_MODE = AUTOMATIC,
    SEEDING_MODE = AUTOMATIC
),
N'SQLNode2' WITH (
    ENDPOINT_URL = N'TCP://SQLNode2.domain.com:5022',
    AVAILABILITY_MODE = SYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT,
    FAILOVER_MODE = AUTOMATIC,
    SEEDING_MODE = AUTOMATIC
);"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Join Secondary Replicas"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Connect to the secondary replica instance (SQLNode2) and execute the following commands to join the availability group and the database."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP [AG01] JOIN;
ALTER DATABASE [SalesDB] SET HADR AVAILABILITY GROUP = [AG01];"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Verification and Monitoring"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"To verify the state of your Availability Group, you can use the Dynamic Management View (DMV) query below."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"SELECT 
    ag.name AS [AG Name],
    ar.replica_server_name AS [Replica],
    rs.role_desc AS [Role],
    rd.synchronization_state_desc AS [Sync State]
FROM sys.availability_groups ag
JOIN sys.availability_replicas ar ON ag.group_id = ar.group_id
JOIN sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states rs ON ar.replica_id = rs.replica_id
JOIN sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states rd ON rs.replica_id = rd.replica_id;"}]
